claims.text: Jira offers a free plan for up to 10 users.
Jira's Standard plan costs $7.91 per user per month and Premium costs $14.54 per user per month for up to 300 users.
Jira's paid Standard plan is $7 per user per month and Premium is $12 per user per month.
Annual billing reduces Jira's Standard plan to $6.52 per user per month for a 300-user team.
Jira Data Center pricing starts at $51,000 per year for 500 or more users.
Jira Enterprise is available at custom pricing with advanced analytics, enhanced security, and support for multiple instances.
Monthly billing raises Jira's Standard plan to $8.15 per user per month and Premium to $15.25 per user per month.
Jira Software Standard starts at $8.15 per user per month billed annually for 1 to 10 users, dropping to roughly $7.16 per user per month for 11 to 100 users.
Jira Software Premium starts at $16 per user per month billed annually for 1 to 10 users.
Jira Enterprise is sold only through sales on annual billing and supports up to 100,000 users per site.
Jira pricing includes hidden costs from paid add-ons in the Atlassian marketplace.
Single sign-on, SCIM, and Active Directory sync require a separate Atlassian Guard Standard subscription for the Free, Standard, and Premium plans, but are included in the Enterprise plan.
Jira provides native time tracking for logging, estimating, and reporting time spent on issues and projects.
Jira's default Time Tracking Report displays time estimates, time spent, and remaining time.
Time entries in Jira can be tracked in minutes, hours, days, or weeks.
The Enterprise plan includes unlimited automation rules and advanced analytics through Atlassian Analytics.
Work item-level security is available to restrict visibility and editing to specific users or groups.
Support for multiple identity providers is available for SAML SSO and SCIM user provisioning.
Jira AI (Atlassian Intelligence) can summarize epics, auto-generate acceptance criteria, suggest issue estimates, and translate natural language into Jira Query Language.
Atlassian announced Jira Data Center will reach end of life on March 28, 2029, new license sales ended on March 30, 2026, and renewals are allowed until March 30, 2028.
Jira is perceived as having a steep learning curve and higher costs, leading some teams to seek alternatives.
Trello is identified as a strong Jira alternative for budget-conscious teams, and monday work management is viewed as easier to use.
Linear is viewed as winning on speed, simplicity, and developer experience, while Jira is viewed as winning on breadth, enterprise readiness, and customization.
Linear provides core agent features on every plan and automatic GitHub issue linking, whereas Jira's sprint automation depends more on deployment type and Marketplace apps.
Jira is recommended for organizations with over 50 engineers that run formal Scrum ceremonies, need stakeholder reporting, and are already in the Atlassian ecosystem.
Monday.com handles cross-functional work well, though sprint-driven teams encounter manual limitations.
Jira offers a Linked Issues feature with explicit relationships such as blocks, is blocked by, and clone of, compared with simpler dependency fields in Asana.
Atlassian launched new Jira features for agentic software engineering workflows in September 2026, introducing an Agent Usage Dashboard.
The Jira Summer 2026 release added 15 new capabilities, including a merged List and All Work view, rebuilt software boards, and AI-assisted planning.
GitHub Copilot for Jira became generally available in June 2026 with features such as streaming agent progress, model selection, and Confluence context.
Jira's free plan was rated among the best free project management software plans available.
Jira received an overall rating of 4 out of 5, with product design rated 5 out of 5 and integrations rated 5 out of 5.
Reviewers of Confluence highlighted native Jira integration as a factor that elevates the tool above a plain wiki and reduces new developer onboarding time.
Jira's Standard plan costs $9.05 per user per month for up to 100,000 users, while Premium costs $18.30 per user per month, both on monthly billing for 1 to 100 users. (judge: contradicted)

ClickUp is viewed as offering more advanced project management features and higher customization than Jira, including real-time chat, document creation, whiteboards, and mind maps that Jira does not match in extent. (judge: not_stated)
Fireship stated that Jira is widely disliked yet difficult to replace in large organizations, and that Linear represents a fresh start using modern UX principles. (judge: not_stated)
Jira is rated highly for structured work management, creation and assignment, issue tracking, and task prioritization. (judge: not_stated)
Jira received its lowest feature ratings for newer AI-driven capabilities. (judge: not_stated)
Jira is most widely adopted in IT services and computer software industries. (judge: not_stated)
Zeen Rachidi published a positive review of Cursor's Jira integration, describing it as five stars with no notes. (judge: contradicted)
